text: Does a moving vibe carry spin one half and the minus sign under exchange through the knit's own stream, rather than as an input?
description:
OP-08: spin-statistics through the rule.

Known: the turning weave does not carry the spinor sign: the coin directions are a 2T torsor, the turn lifts after four beats to (-1, +1) in $SU(2)_L \times SU(2)_R$, and the palindromic schedule nets +1 where the rejected cyclic one nets -1 (E-SPN-0044). The role carries it: under the 2 pi turn every role is a spin one half doublet and a scalar, the turn lifting to -P in Sigma(648) (E-SPN-0051, E-SPN-0054). A full turn of a cluster is $(-1)^N$ with N the doublet count, the model's fermion number, and with every role locked into its doublet every charge-one state is spinorial, so turn sign and exchange sign agree (E-SPN-0071). A moving token is a spinor by force: no husk-covariant stream can copy the scalar line (E-SPN-0066). Exclusion lives in the signed weight: the fermion pair on the role grid is 72 loves and 18 fears, every fear on a coincident point (E-SPN-0045). E-SPN-0014 computes an identity true of every vector, and its exchange signs were typed.

Unknown: the doublet-locked stream in the knit itself, adopted on 2026-09-26 and not built: the adopted knit copies all 24 roots at once, so its copies commute and the spin never enters the band (E-SPN-0083). The tokens of E-SPN-0066 and E-SPN-0071 are stand-ins.

Why it matters: the published paper claimed it.

Scope: open research.

Skills: representation theory, quantum foundations.

Where to start: test/experiment/spin/fermi-exclusion.ts.

The claims it would move: R-FND-0001.

Evidence named: paper errata, E-SPN-0014, E-SPN-0044, E-SPN-0045, E-SPN-0051, E-SPN-0054, E-SPN-0066, E-SPN-0071, E-SPN-0083.
